arxiv-1911-03268.title: Inducing brain-relevant bias in natural language processing models
arxiv-1911-03268.creator: Dan Schwartz, Mariya Toneva, Leila Wehbe
arxiv-1911-03268.description: Abstract Progress in natural language processing (NLP) models that estimate representations of word sequences has recently been leveraged to improve the understanding of language processing in the brain. However, these models have not been specifically designed to capture the way the brain represents language meaning.

arxiv-2308-12498.title: Quiet, but not silent: Uncovering quiescent state properties of two transient High Mass X-ray binaries Quiet, but not silent: Uncovering quiescent state properties of two transient High Mass X-ray binaries – References
arxiv-2308-12498.creator: Gayathri Raman, Varun, Pragati Pradhan, Jamie Kennea
arxiv-2308-12498.description: Abstract We present the first set of broadband spectral and timing studies of two transient X-ray pulsars, MXB 0656-072 and MAXI J1409-619 using NuSTAR observations conducted during quiescence. Despite being captured at one of their lowest luminosity states, both these targets show signs of ongoing low-level accretion.

arxiv-2410-11716.title: Randomization-based Inference for MCP-Mod
arxiv-2410-11716.creator: Lukas Pin, Oleksandr Sverdlov, Frank Bretz, Björn Bornkamp
arxiv-2410-11716.description: Abstract Dose selection is critical in pharmaceutical drug development, as it directly impacts therapeutic efficacy and patient safety of a drug. The Generalized Multiple Comparison Procedures and Modeling (MCP-Mod) approach is commonly used in Phase II trials for testing and estimation of dose-response relationships.

arxiv-2410-20392.title: The McKay Conjecture on character degrees
arxiv-2410-20392.creator: Marc Cabanes, Britta Späth
arxiv-2410-20392.description: Abstract We prove that for any prime ℓ \ell , any finite group has as many irreducible complex characters of degree prime to ℓ \ell as the normalizers of its Sylow ℓ \ell -subgroups. This equality was conjectured by John McKay.

arxiv-2502-13637.title: Exploring Mutual Cross-Modal Attention for Context-Aware Human Affordance Generation
arxiv-2502-13637.creator: Prasun Roy, Saumik Bhattacharya, Subhankar Ghosh, Umapada Pal, and Michael Blumenstein
arxiv-2502-13637.description: Abstract Human affordance learning investigates contextually relevant novel pose prediction such that the estimated pose represents a valid human action within the scene. While the task is fundamental to machine perception and automated interactive navigation agents, the exponentially large number of probable pose and action variations make the problem challenging and non-trivial.

arxiv-2503-05284.title: Flux-tunable parity-protected qubit based on a single full-shell nanowire Josephson junction
arxiv-2503-05284.creator: G. Giavaras, Rubén Seoane Souto, Maria José Calderón, Ramón Aguado
arxiv-2503-05284.description: Abstract Leveraging the higher harmonics content of the Josephson potential in a superconducting circuit offers a promising route in the search for new qubits with increased protection against decoherence. In this work, we demonstrate how the flux tunability of a hybrid semiconductor-superconductor Josephson junction based on a single full-shell nanowire enables this possibility.

arxiv-2508-19963.title: Flocking Behavior: An Innovative Inspiration for the Optimization of Production Plants
arxiv-2508-19963.creator: M. Umlauft and M. Schranz
arxiv-2508-19963.description: Abstract Optimizing modern production plants using the job-shop principle is a known hard problem. For very large plants, like semiconductor fabs, the problem becomes unsolvable on a plant-wide scale in a reasonable amount of time using classical linear optimization. An alternative approach is the use of swarm intelligence algorithms.

arxiv-2512-05242.title: Learning to Code with Context: A Study-Based Approach
arxiv-2512-05242.creator: Uwe M. Borghoff, Mark Minas, Jannis Schopp
arxiv-2512-05242.description: Abstract The rapid emergence of generative AI tools is transforming the way software is developed. Consequently, software engineering education must adapt to ensure that students not only learn traditional development methods but also understand how to meaningfully and responsibly use these new technologies.

pmc-11386333.title: Lipid droplets and small extracellular vesicles: More than two independent entities
pmc-11386333.creator: Géraldine C Genard, Luca Tirinato, Francesca Pagliari, Jessica Da Silva, Alessandro Giammona, Fatema Alquraish, Maria Parra Reyes, Marie Bordas, Maria Grazia Marafioti, Simone Di Franco, Jeannette Janssen, Daniel Garcia‐Calderón, Rachel Hanley, Clelia Nistico, Yoshinori Fukasawa, Torsten Müller, Jer
pmc-11386333.description: Despite increasing knowledge about small extracellular vesicle (sEV) composition and functions in cell–cell communication, the mechanism behind their biogenesis remains unclear. Here, we reveal for the first time that sEV biogenesis and release into the microenvironment are tightly connected with another important organelle, Lipid Droplets (LDs).

pmc-11551630.title: Pathologic complete response to conversion therapy in hepatocellular carcinoma using patient-derived organoids: A case report
pmc-11551630.creator: Yong-Gang He, Zheng Wang, Jing Li, Wang Xi, Chong-Yu Zhao, Xiao-Bing Huang, Lu Zheng
pmc-11551630.description: BACKGROUNDFor primary liver cancer, the key to conversion therapy depends on the effectiveness of drug treatment. Patient-derived tumor organoids have been demonstrated to improve the efficacy of conversion therapy by identifying individual-targeted effective drugs, but their clinical effects in liver cancer remain unknown.

pmc-12413337.title: Interdisciplinary evidence-based tumor board simulation training in surgical medical education
pmc-12413337.creator: Nora Corinna Altmayer, Elias Khajeh, Johanna Fellhofer-Hofer, Anna Lintner, Matthias Alexander Fink, Constantin Schwab, Niels Halama, Felix Nickel, Arianeb Mehrabi, Fee Klupp
pmc-12413337.description: PurposeEvidence-based medicine (EBM), precision medicine and interdisciplinarity are becoming increasingly important in medical education. The purposeful connection between EBM and interdisciplinary work is given in the context of a tumor board, since therapy decisions are discussed here in an interdisciplinary team based on current evidence-based guidelines. To date, there has been little focus on either topic.

pmc-12539060.title: Correction: A plan or pandemonium? The conundrum of retrotransposon activation in cancer
pmc-12539060.creator: Elina Zueva
pmc-12539060.description:
A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). h high-resolution figures; and the omitted part for Fig. 4 caption was inserted. The complete caption for Fig. 4 is given below:

Figure 4. Schematic representation of the potentially dual role of ERE sequences in cancer initiation and progression. In early malignant transformation, the activity of EREs may promote the elimination of pre-cancerous clones through LINE-1-induced genotoxic stress, sensing of ERE-derived oligonucleotides, engagement of adaptive immunity against ERE-encoded epitopes, and the generation of non-functional oncogenic isoforms via aberrant splicing or promoter activity.

pmc-12614886.title: Prokaryotic expression, polyclonal antibody production, and application of yak TGF-β2
pmc-12614886.creator: Yaming Chen, Yangyang Pan, Sijiu Yu, Jinglei Wang, Jiangfeng Fan
pmc-12614886.description: This study aimed to generate yak-specific polyclonal antibodies against transforming growth factor beta 2 (TGF-β2). Specific primers targeting the TGF-β2 coding sequence (CDS) were designed, and the gene was amplified via RT-PCR. The amplified product was cloned into the pET-32a(+) vector to construct the recombinant plasmid pET-32a(+)-TGF-β2. This plasmid was transformed into Escherichia coli BL21(DE3) for protein expression.

pmc-12737235.title: A Hybrid Search Behavior-Based Adaptive Grey Wolf Optimizer for Cooperative Path Planning for Multiple UAVs
pmc-12737235.creator: Zhiwen Zheng, Hao Huang, Chenbo Li, Yongbin Yu, Xiangxiang Wang, Jingye Cai, Xi Huang, Songbo Hu, Jonghoek Kim, Bingbing Gao
pmc-12737235.description: Cooperative path planning of multiple unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) is pivotal for improving mission efficiency and safety in complex scenarios. However, the multi-constraint of UAVs increases the design difficulity of cooperative path planning. To address these issues, a hybrid search behavior-based adaptive grey wolf optimizer (HSB-GWO) is proposed in this work.

pmc-13094333.title: Dkk1 inhibition restores mandibular growth in an achondroplasia mouse model
pmc-13094333.creator: Briantana Raveendranathan, Valentin Estibals, Eric Pulido, Clara Lemoine, Nabil Kaci, Rachel Pereur, Mohammed Zarhrate, Sébastien Dupichaud, Emilie Dambroise, Laurence Legeai-Mallet, Martin Biosse Duplan
pmc-13094333.description: Meckel's and condylar cartilages are key to mandible development, with Meckel's cartilage acting as a template and condylar cartilage as a growth center. In achondroplasia, the most common form of genetic dwarfism, abnormalities of these cartilages lead to micrognathia, with significant functional repercussions for affected individuals. How FGFR3 overactivation in achondroplasia disrupts Meckel's and condylar cartilages is largely unknown.

pmc-13111265.title: Deciphering the peripheral immune landscape of Alzheimer’s disease through integrated multi-omics research and cohort validation
pmc-13111265.creator: Shi Lv, Jin-yi Kuang, Tian-wei Wang, Li-ping Zhang, Jian Liu, Wen-di Wang, Ming-feng Yang, Qing-bin Ni, Bao-liang Sun, Jing-yi Sun
pmc-13111265.description: ObjectiveThis study investigated molecular drivers of AD-associated peripheral immune dysregulation to identify pathogenic genes and therapeutic targets for precision diagnosis and intervention.MethodsA large-scale GWAS meta-analysis (n = 894,710) was performed, followed by two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR) using multi-tissue cis-eQTL data to identify putative causal genes.

pmc-13152808.title: Bridging therapy before CAR-T for multiple myeloma: a survey from the CMWP and CTIWP of the EBMT
pmc-13152808.creator: Nico Gagelmann, Maximilian Merz, Laurien G A Baaij, Linda Koster, Jorinde D Hoogenboom, Joanna Drozd-Sokolowska, Kavita Raj, Jürgen Kuball, Patrick J Hayden, Florent Malard, Laurent Garderet, Annalisa Ruggeri, Donal McLornan
pmc-13152808.description: aiting infusion [1]. However, practices remain highly individualized, with choices driven by disease tempo, prior therapies, comorbidities, and center experience [2]. Furthermore, pivotal trials allowed only limited regimens, leaving a gap between trial constraints and the breadth of strategies used in practice [3–5].

pmc-13234500.title: Heterogeneity in kinesiophobia among postoperative aortic dissection survivors: associations with exercise self-efficacy, family support, and coping styles
pmc-13234500.creator: Xin Yang, Yuan Luo, Dan Wang
pmc-13234500.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundEarly postoperative kinesiophobia in aortic dissection survivors is associated with reduced exercise adherence, worsening physical and mental health, and diminished quality of life. This study aimed to identify kinesiophobia subtypes 1 month after surgery and to explore the associative pathways linking exercise self-efficacy, family support, coping styles, and kinesiophobia, thereby providing a theoretical basis for the future development of targeted interventions.MethodsThis cross-sectional study enrolled 309 aortic dissection survivors (September 2024–July 2025) from three university hospitals 1 month post-surgery.

pmc-13272036.title: LUCAT1 promotes stemness in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma by sponging miR-128
pmc-13272036.creator: Yifan Wen, Shuo Liu, Yaqing Mao, Ruifeng Li, Hui Yuh Soh, Yao Yu, Wen-bo Zhang, Lingfei Jia, Xin Peng
pmc-13272036.description: Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) progression is well documented to be predominantly driven by a small subset of cancer stem cells (CSCs). These CSCs are implicated in recurrence, metastasis, dormancy, and therapy resistance. Therefore, targeting cancer stem cells has inspired the design of innovative treatment strategies.

pmc-13349781.title: Dietary intake adequacy among Iranian older adults: evidence from national household survey data and two population-based cohorts
pmc-13349781.creator: Ali Shokri, Nasrin Omidvar, Delaram Ghodsi, Hassan Eini-Zinab, Farshad Sharifi, Arezoo Rezazadeh

pmc-13440369.title: Unveiling the Ultralow Thermal Conductivity of Hybrid Perovskites
pmc-13440369.creator: Qinqin He, Yuli Chen, Zhigang Li, Yanguang Zhou
pmc-13440369.description: Hybrid perovskites are among the most important photon‐to‐electricity materials, whose performance is strongly limited by poor heat dissipation. This is due to their significantly low thermal conductivity, and the origin of such low thermal conductivity is still in debate and much less well‐documented.

pmc-13654928.title: Observation and modeling of fertility loss attributable to natural disasters from 1990-2021
pmc-13654928.creator: Manman Chen, Wanzhou Wang, Din Son Tan, Zichen Ye, Yuankai Zhao, Ze Liang, Xijie Wang, Juan Juan, Chao Yang
pmc-13654928.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundNatural disasters have increasingly threatened population health, but their global impacts on fertility remain uncertain. This study aims to quantify global fertility loss attributable to natural disasters and its socioeconomic disparities.MethodsWe conducted a two-stage analysis using disaster records from the Emergency Events Database (EM-DAT) and total fertility rate (TFR) and net reproductive rate (NRR) data from the Global Burden of Disease (GBD) 2021 database. First, we used country-year panel data to assess exposure-response functions.
